# Make the dock WorkspaceSet adapter overridable through Neo

## Context

The remaining extension question on #18304 names `WorkspaceSet` as a bounded candidate. Its [parent record](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18304#issuecomment-5564654865) already rejects a registered wrapper that copies factory descriptors after class setup: registration succeeds while the copied method shadows the configured override.

## The Problem

At `dev@5c75b2d666`, `src/dashboard/dock/window/WorkspaceSet.mjs` still exports `createDockWorkspaceSet`, returning an object whose methods close over manager and Group resolvers. A direct probe against the identical source blob `47880b2eb98ae24eaeaefc63ce44ed1c917041a9` produced:

```text
factory namespace: null; configured has override: not reached
registered Base control namespace: present; configured has override: reached
```

Workstation and Demo-B each construct this adapter. Popups borrow the root's adapter. A class conversion introduces a real instance lifetime: neither creating consumer currently destroys this plain object.

## The Architectural Reality

`Neo.setupClass` applies overwrites to the prototype; `core.Base.destroy` unregisters the instance and clears its own fields. `window/VesselPark.mjs` is the neighbouring registered-owner precedent. Group participant membership belongs to `manager.Transaction`, not to this adapter. Registration callbacks may outlive the adapter that created them.

## The Fix

Convert the existing module to `Neo.dashboard.dock.window.WorkspaceSet extends Neo.core.Base`, default-exported through `Neo.setupClass`. Put the actual operations on the prototype. Replace the factory imports and calls in both production constructors and existing tests. The creating consumers destroy their adapter; borrowed popup references do not.

Keep Group participant callbacks bound to their registration context so clearing adapter fields cannot break retained capture, preparation, adoption, compensation or projection. Preserve current membership, validation, queue-head reduction and write receipts.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Module construction | `WorkspaceSet.mjs#createDockWorkspaceSet`; `Neo.setupClass` | Default registered class, created through Neo with manager/getGroupId/documentModel | No compatibility factory | Class/config JSDoc | Namespace plus effective overwrite/subclass dispatch |
| Existing methods and size | Current WorkspaceSet implementation | Same arguments/results; real prototype dispatch | Existing unbound/refusal behavior | Method JSDoc | Existing membership, compensation and transaction suites |
| Adapter destruction | `core.Base.destroy`; creator teardown in Workstation/Demo-B | Release adapter instance only; creator owns teardown | No implicit participant retirement | Lifetime JSDoc | Instance released; retained participants remain usable |
| Registered participant callbacks | `WorkspaceSet.register`; Group participant lifetime | Retain their registration dependencies independently of adapter fields | Existing validation/refusal behavior | Registration JSDoc | Queued and later writes after adapter destruction, including projection |

## Decision Record impact

Aligned with ADR 0029 §2.1: windows remain render targets, membership remains worker-owned. No schema, Group or transaction protocol amendment. This is a leaf of the already-graduated ownership direction on #18304.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The default export registers the WorkspaceSet class, and an actual method override changes dispatch; no copied post-setup descriptor can shadow it.
- [ ] Both production constructors use the registered class; the named factory export and its executable consumers are removed.
- [ ] Workstation and Demo-B release the adapter they create; borrowed popup teardown does not destroy it.
- [ ] Destroying an adapter does not unregister Group participants or break their already-registered capture/prepare/adopt/compensate/project callbacks, including queued work.
- [ ] Existing membership, synchronous compensation, queued transaction, placement, participation and consumer tests remain green.
- [ ] Modified APIs retain JSDoc summaries and the generated class hierarchy includes the new class.

## Out of Scope

TearOut conversion, additional consumer decomposition, `#18448`'s multi-step pin repair, changed transaction semantics, new persisted state, and guide authoring.

## Avoided Traps

- A namespace-only wrapper is a false green; the prototype must own the executed methods.
- Destroying the adapter must not retire the Group or borrowed participants.
- Do not bind retained callbacks to fields that Base destruction clears.
- Do not preserve an unused factory for compatibility or introduce another manager.
